answer: New identities join mutual-insurance pools of, say, twelve members who stake together; if one member is proven a sybil, the whole pool's stake is slashed. The river of rewards only flows to pools whose members keep each other clean, because fraud is like a glacier — slow to surface, but it never stays buried. Peers audit one another far cheaper than the network ever could, and no sock-puppet can wander into a group unnoticed: a single exposed fake identity wipes out every identity in its pool, so scaling the attack multiplies the farmer's own losses instead of its gains.
